newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude down, ample supply amid few buyers.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude down, ample supply amid few buyers.

text.p: Asian crude prices were weaker on Wednesday, weighed down by an amply supplied physical market, traders said.
A handful of Oman and Dubai cargoes remained available for the May spot market, putting pressure on the more sour grades.
Traders said Oman would find buyers retreating to MPM -10 cents, although sellers were expected to hold off until the release of Oman's March official selling price.
Dubai remained under pressure of converting to a contango market. Asian brokers found the May/June market at -12/-7 cents and June/July at flat/+7 cents.
This compared with flat/+4 cents and +5/+11 cents on Tuesday.
Two U.S. majors said they had finished trading May MidEast barrels but a third major said it still had buying requirements.

Chinese refineries have appeared on the scene this week to buy Minas. Traders said this reflected refineries, such as the WEPEC, buying for when they restart operations following scheduled turnarounds.
The flurry of Minas deals have largely been between ICP -15/-10 cents, although one deal was heard as high as ICP -6 cents.
The deepening contango on the Brent market has made Masila crude more attractive, traders said.
Dated Brent was valued at -$1.00/-$0.90 to the May market owing to the soft Brent physical market.

A U.S. major sold 450,000 barrels of May Masila to a Japanese trader at Dated Brent less around 40 cents. The term players achieved therefore around a 10-cent gain over second quarter OSP of dated -50 cents.
A second deal, between a European major and a U.S. refiner, was achieved at Dated Brent -45/-40 cents, traders said.
